findings.issue: In the per-line-up loop, `kept.every((h) => h.lineUp === lineUp)` is vacuously true for Mixed and Soft because the fixture has no such hands; only the `not.toContain(bare)` line does work there.
findings.evidence: data.hands has only Tough, Custom and a bare hand; filterTrendData(..., Mixed|Soft).hands is [].
findings.fix: Optionally assert the exact kept lists per line-up (e.g. Custom -> [custom], Mixed/Soft -> []) instead of the every() check.

summary: Implementation matches the spec exactly: optional lineUp on TrendHand/TrendSource/TrendFilter, LINE_UP_LABEL/LINE_UP_OPTIONS from LineUpName, ALL_TRENDS.lineUp='all', trendHand copies lineUp only when present, filterTrendData ANDs a per-hand lineUp predicate with missing filter lineUp treated as All and still returns `data` itself for All/All/All (and for legacy {tableSize, gameType} literals). The select (#stats-line-up) sits between Game type and Group by inside the view-gated filter row; App.tsx is untouched and its existing ALL_TRENDS reset covers reopening, which the e2e verifies through the real App. Tests feed reversed/shuffled records, recompute values from HandRecord.decisions, and would catch the obvious mutations: ignoring lineUp (hand counts 1100/550/0 fail), ignoring table size (1400 vs 1100), using the session record's config.lineUp (fixtures override lineUp on hand records only, so Custom/Tough sessions carry a different config.lineUp, and the e2e Custom view would show 0 hands), or computing G-2 from the filtered set (7.5 vs 3.1, both groupings). The AC#3 reorder of session starts (HU Mixed, Tough 6-max, Mixed 6-max cash, Mixed 6-max SNG) is sound: SPEC-03 only requires start order != id order (ids 9,2,7,4 satisfy that) and does not mandate the table row order as start order; with the table's row order the Mixed 6-max cash session would start first, so the first 500 cash hands (the sole BB/100 point) and the first Major point would be identical across the combined, Mixed-only and 6-max-only views, making the spec's 'these points differ' assertion impossible for bb100. The reorder makes that comparison meaningful without weakening any equality check. Vitest files (31 tests) and the Playwright spec (Chromium + WebKit) pass locally; gate fix-2 is green. Only a NIT on a partially vacuous unit assertion.
